LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P1.Title: 1. Chess
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P1.Body:
There is one goal — **leave the enemy king with nowhere to go.** That is checkmate, and the game ends the moment it happens.

The king is never actually captured. Moves that would allow it are not legal moves at all. If you have no legal move and your king is under attack, you have lost; if you have no legal move and it is not, the game is drawn.

The figure shows White holding the back rank with a single rook. The king's own pawns block the way out.
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P2.Title: 2. How the pieces move
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P2.Body:
**Pawns** go one square forward, two on their first move, and capture only on the diagonal.

**Rooks** run along ranks and files, **bishops** along diagonals, **queens** along both. The **king** moves one square in any direction.

The **knight** is the odd one — it jumps in an L and does not care what stands in between. The dots in the figure are every square one knight can reach.
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P3.Title: 3. Playing a move
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P3.Body:
Click a piece and its legal squares are marked with dots. A red ring means something of theirs is standing there. Click the square to play the move.

To castle, move the king two squares sideways; the rook follows on its own. En passant simply shows up as a legal square, so there is nothing extra to remember.

When a pawn reaches the far rank you are asked what it becomes. Usually a queen. Usually.
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P4.Title: 4. Colours and taking it back
LanguageData.CHS.Tut.P4.Body:
Your colour changes from game to game. With Black the opponent moves first and the board is shown from your side. You can pin yourself to White in the settings.

Undo steps back two moves — yours and their answer. On the harder tiers it may be blocked, depending on your settings.

An unfinished game stays on the chess table. Sit down again and it picks up where it stopped.
